editorial.headline: Textile Goods Beyond Apparel, Open Nationally and Workable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers finished textile goods such as flags, banners, pennants, and textile life-saving floats or jackets, with registration open across all listed business scales.
editorial.body:
KBLI 13929 is a manufacturing classification for finished textile goods that are not ready-made clothing. The record describes a practical, object-based activity: making other completed textile products such as flags, banners, pennants, and textile life-saving floats or jackets. The common thread is not fashion or garment retail, but the production of textile articles that leave the workshop as finished goods for public display, institutional use, commercial signage, safety use, or comparable non-apparel purposes.

That makes the code broad, but not vague. It is for businesses whose real work is textile fabrication into usable objects: cutting, assembling, finishing, and preparing the kind of textile goods named in the scope. A founder should read the classification through that manufacturing lens. If the business is registering this activity, the centre of gravity is the making of the textile item itself, not a separate service, trading activity, or another line outside the record. The slim record also states that the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses, so the same activity can be registered from a small producer up to a large-scale operation, provided the registered activity remains within the stated scope.

The national foreign-investment position is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to the listed Perpres instruments. In plain English, the national classification is foreign-open, and the foreign-ownership ceiling shown in the record is 100%. There is no lower foreign cap in the slim record, and there is no separate qualification, capital threshold, licence detail, or timeline stated here. The responsible reading is therefore simple: nationally, this is an open PMA activity according to the data provided.

The Bali picture is also unusually important because the record includes the island-side moratorium logic. Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, under the listed governor-letter source. But this record does **not** mark KBLI 13929 as blocked in Bali. The record assigns Bali the status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, explaining it as: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest conclusion is not that Bali adds a separate percentage cap, partnership condition, or quota; none appears in the record. The conclusion is narrower and stronger: this activity is nationally foreign-open, and the slim record does not block PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium because of the stated higher-risk treatment at large scale.
editorial.pullQuote: The responsible reading is simple: nationally, this is an open PMA activity, and the slim record does not block it in Bali under the moratorium.
